transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-05
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Mark R (Sundial CTO), Lisa C (Platform), Omar F (Security), Talia G (PM)

Summary (auto): quick walkthrough of org vs project API keys, how to enforce per-project token quotas and rate limits via the Console and Optimize recommendations; discuss Dedicated vs Hosted for predictable quotas; confirm security requirements and pilot scope.

00:00 Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for making time, quick roll call?
00:06 Mark: Mark here.
00:07 Lisa: Lisa here.
00:09 Omar: Omar.
00:11 Talia: Talia.
00:12 Alex: Great. Priya and Jordan from the infra team will do the product demo, I'll cover pricing/next steps.
00:20 Priya: Cool, so I'm gonna share my screen — hopping into the Redwood Console. if you see anything weird let me know, screen-sharing lag sometimes.
00:32 Jordan: we'll jump to the org settings first — this is where you create the org-level API key and then you can carve out project keys underneath it.
00:42 Lisa: quick question, is the org key used for billing across projects or can billing be per project?
00:47 Alex: you can do both — usage tagged per project for chargeback, but you can also have a single billing entity. We'll show the cost breakdown in the Console usage view.
00:56 Priya: OK looking at the org page — here's the org key; note we recommend not using the org key directly in client apps, it's more of a management-level credential.
01:10 Priya: Now under Projects we have Project A, B, and C — you can mint project keys with scoped permissions. you can choose quota profiles at creation time.
01:23 Mark: Scoped permissions like read-only embeddings vs full generate?
01:26 Priya: yeah exactly, you can scope operations (generate/chat/embeddings), per-model access, and even per-route time windows.
01:36 Jordan: showing the Quotas tab — we have rate limits (requests per minute / tokens per minute) and absolute monthly quotas. You can click "Create quota profile".
01:46 01:46 Lisa: if we set a low burst for a project, will it automatically queue requests or return 429s?
01:53 Priya: good question — by default we return a 429 when the rate limit is exceeded. You can configure a soft-throttle that will queue short spikes for up to configured window; that's what our burst buffer is for. there's a per-project burst bucket.
02:07 Omar: what about fallback routing — if project hits quota can it fall back to a lower-cost model or different region?
02:13 Jordan: yes, you can define fallback policies at the org level — e.g., if rx model x is saturated, route to a compatible quantized variant; or route to a different capacity pool. We also have a policy for routing to Dedicated vs Hosted based on tier.
02:25 Talia: can we assign quotas by team instead of project? our org structure maps teams->projects.
02:31 Priya: you can namespace keys however you like. Some customers create a project per team and then attach quota profiles. Others use project keys to map features. it's flexible.
02:41 Alex: quick qualification — what's your target go-live for this pilot?
02:44 Mark: we'd like to start pilot end of August and evaluate through Sep. So 2-4 weeks.
02:50 Alex: sounds good. we'll align the pilot to three projects per your note.
03:00 Priya: demo continued — setting a rate limit: we'll create a profile "eng-region-us" 100 QPS, 200k tokens/minute, monthly cap 10M tokens, burst 500 requests.
03:15 Lisa: 100 QPS seems high for some of our teams, can we do per-key overrides?
03:20 Priya: yes you can assign a base quota profile at project creation and override per-key. also there's a programmatic API to update limits so you can script adjustments.
03:31 Jordan: pointing out the API: POST /v1/keys/{key_id}/quota with JSON body — note the SDKs wrap this. (minor mis-transcription: actual path shown as /v1/keyz/.. in UI screenshot)
03:45 Omar: on the security side we need key rotation every 30 days and audit logs for key creation/deletion.
03:51 Priya: supported. rotation can be forced client-side or via the Console we can issue a new key and deprecate the old one. Audit logs are retained per your retention policy — we can enable long-retention exports to your S3 or to your SIEM.
04:06 Omar: retention duration — can we get 2 years for compliance?
04:09 Alex: for Private deployments yes; for hosted we have add-ons for extended audit retention — will include in pricing email.
04:17 Lisa: for the pilot we want per-project billing tagged to our internal billing center ID.
04:21 Alex: we can send usage reports with project tags, or you can call our usage APIs and ingest into your billing system.
04:30 Priya: now the Console shows a "simulate" button — we'll run a demo spike using our built-in traffic generator to show burst behavior.
04:38 [04:46] Priya: starting simulated traffic — you should see Project B jump to 600 rps then drop as the burst bucket depletes — look at the live metrics panel.
04:52 Lisa: I see the 429s increasing at 04:50 — okay that's expected.
05:00 Jordan: note the split between token rate limit and request rate limit — if you have small requests but heavy token output you'll hit token limits first.
05:10 Talia: curious about Optimize advice — can Redwood Optimize recommend quotas based on historical traffic?
05:16 Priya: yes, Optimize can analyze telemetry and suggest quota profiles and batching configuration. it'll also estimate cost delta if you move to different quantization or batching.
05:27 Mark: if a project exceeds monthly cap, is it automatically disabled?
05:31 Alex: it's configurable — you can choose hard-stop, grace period with email alerts, or suspend but allow read-only operations. Common pattern is hard-stop for production to avoid runaway cost.
05:42 Omar: how are secrets stored? we need HSM integration and customer-managed KMS for Private deploys.
05:49 Jordan: for Private we support KMS/HSM and can integrate with your key rotation policies. For Hosted we encrypt at rest and provide envelope encryption with bring-your-own-keys option via our KMS partner. minor note the UI sometimes shows KMS as K-M-S spelled out.
06:05 Lisa: latency concerns — if we enable per-project isolation (dedicated pools), will we see lower p95?
06:12 Priya: yes Dedicated pools reduce noisy-neighbor effect; you can also pin certain models to dedicated capacity. There's a tradeoff in unit cost — we'll show sample numbers in the price sheet.
06:22 Mark: can we throttle only some routes? e.g., embedding endpoints vs generation?
06:27 Priya: absolutely — route-level quotas exist. You can also tag calls in the header and run per-route checks.
06:35 Lisa: about SDKs — are quota errors surfaced in SDKs as typed exceptions?
06:39 Jordan: SDK v2 surfaces a QuotaExceeded error with fields rate_limit and retry_after but sometimes the transcript shows it as 'QuotaExceed' in code snippets; the proper exception name will be in docs.
06:50 Omar: on compliance — do you have SOC2 Type II?
06:53 Alex: yes SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 in progress — we'll share certs.
06:58 Talia: what's the difference between org key admin roles vs project roles?
07:02 Priya: org admins can create org-level policies and view billing; project admins can manage project keys and quotas but not org billing or org-wide policies unless explicitly granted. RBAC is fine-grained.
07:15 [07:18] Priya: switching to API demo — show rate limit check endpoint and headers returned (x-rate-limit, x-rate-remaining, x-reset). sometimes the client lib mis-parses reset.
07:33 Lisa: we need SSO/SAML integration for our org login.
07:36 Alex: supported, SSO + SCIM for provisioning. We'll include the SAML metadata doc in the follow-up package.
07:45 Jordan: also showing audit log export settings — you can route to S3, Splunk, or your SIEM. The export includes user, key_id, project, action and IP. minor note: IP geolocation sometimes shows internal NAT address; we recommend agent-side forwarding of client IP.
08:02 Mark: any limits on number of project keys? we have hundreds of micro-services.
08:07 Priya: keys are virtually unlimited but note control plane scaling considerations — we recommend grouping microservices into logical projects if you have thousands.
08:16 Talia: how do we do staged rollouts of quota changes?
08:20 Jordan: you can roll out a quota change as canary on specific keys or projects and watch the telemetry; we also expose a dry-run mode that logs what would have been throttled without enforcing.
08:34 Lisa: can we do rate limiting by IP or client ID rather than key?
08:38 Priya: yes you can set rate limits on custom labels; keys are the primary identity but you can apply additional rate dimensions.
08:46 [09:00] Priya: quick detour — offline policy editor: we keep JSON schemas so infra can check policies in CI.
09:10 Mark: if we do a Dedicated pool for platform features and Hosted for experiments, can we route traffic automatically?
09:15 Alex: yes using routing policies: route by project tag + model compatibility. If Dedicated is full you can failover to Hosted with a cost/latency tradeoff.
09:28 Talia: for the pilot what telemetry will we need to send?
09:33 Priya: request rates, tokens per request, model used, route, and success/error codes. We can give you a small kit and a node/python snippet.
09:45 [10:00] Priya: now I'll flip to the Optimize panel — it shows suggested quota profile based on last 30 days; it recommended lowering token cap for Project C and enabling prefix caching for repeated prompts.
10:12 Lisa: prefix caching — is that safe when prompts include PII?
10:15 Priya: you control caching scope; for PII-heavy workloads you can disable prefix cache or enable ephemeral caching with very short TTLs. We also support redaction rules at the request layer.
10:29 Omar: will caching keep sensitive data? what about encryption at rest for cache?
10:33 Jordan: KV cache is encrypted and for Private deploys can live in your VPC; for hosted there's an option to disable caching altogether. sometimes the transcriber shows K-V cash instead of KV cache but it's the same thing.
10:46 Mark: walk me through a failure scenario — project exceeds monthly quota in middle of business day.
10:50 Priya: alerting: we emit telemetry and can trigger PagerDuty, slack alerts; options: hard-stop, soft-stop with email to project owners, or on-exceed route to degraded model. We demoed this in the sim earlier.
11:05 Lisa: what about cost control — can we pre-commit capacity for projects?
11:09 Alex: you can reserve Dedicated capacity per project pool; otherwise Reserved capacity is org-level and you can carve quotas against it. we'll include sample calculations for unit cost and committed discounts.
11:20 Talia: any rate-limit token math we should know? like token/min vs tokens/request conversions?
11:25 Priya: we provide conversion estimates and examples in the docs. Optimize will estimate tokens per call based on your prompt shapes.
11:35 Jordan: showing API headers again — X-Redwood-Quota, X-Redwood-Remaining etc. SDK surfaces these.
11:44 [11:50] Alex: ok gonna switch to next steps — we'll send pricing and security pack, Priya will send the console clip, and you (Mark) will share traffic CSV. We'll get a security deep-dive with Omar next week.
12:02 Mark: sounds good. quick ask — can you include a sample policy JSON and a terraform snippet?
12:08 Priya: yes we'll include a policy example and a terraform provider snippet that shows quota profile creation.
12:15 Omar: we may want to run an initial perf test — can Redwood run a runbook or do we need to use your stress tool?
12:20 Jordan: we can run a joint benchmark or provide the stress tool for you to run in your environment; we'll coordinate in the pilot kickoff.
12:30 Talia: thanks everyone, that was helpful.
12:32 Alex: thank you appreciate it, we'll follow up by Friday with attachments.
12:36 [closing] 16:54 UTC end
